text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet and his Hungarian counterpart Gyula Horn have agreed to boost economic co-operation and bilateral ties following talks in Budapest on Tuesday.
-- Vietnam Airlines will increase its flights from Ho Chi Minh City to Osaka to five per week.
-- The Government has approved plans for the repayment of $130 million in foreign debt in cash and goods this year to nine countries including Russia, Poland, and Slovakia.
-- Vietnam and Britain should sign a trade and investment protection agreement to help ties between the two countries, Britain's new ambassador to Vietnam said on Wednesday.
-- The Ministry of Planning and Investment (MPI) licensed 14 foreign direct investment projects worth $233.4 million in May.
-- The Government has appointed Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development Nguyen Cong Tan to head a committee for natural disasters.
-- Inflation in Vietnam in the first five months of this year increased by one percent.

-- The last U.N chartered voluntary repatriation flights carrying 245 boatpeople from Hong kong arrived in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City on Wednesday. About 600 people are estimated left in Hong Kong and are due to repatriated before June 30.
-- Vietnam's industrial production growth increased by 13.7 percent in the first five months of this year compared with the same period last year.
-- A Cuban Foreign Ministry delegation began a four-day working visit to Vietnam on Tuesday.
